title: Kia Accelerates Its Connection with New Generations by Entering the Esports Ecosystem Through League of Legends in Latin America
summary: Kia Accelerates Its Connection with New Generations by Entering the Esports Ecosystem Through League of Legends in Latin America  WebWire
content:
Kia Central & South America has become an official sponsor of the LCS and CBLOL, two of the most important League of Legends leagues in the Americas

The partnership strengthens the brands connection with an industry that brings together more than 300 million players across Latin America

Kia launches Runes to Road, a regional activation designed to bring League of Legends fans closer to the action

title: Has Fearless Draft actually improved champion diversity in League of Legends?
summary: Has Fearless Draft actually improved champion diversity in League of Legends?  Esports Insider
content:
Hajrudin Krdzic is a gaming and esports writer with over five years of experience covering live-service updates and competitive scenes. His first love was RTS games, which naturally grew into a long-term passion for MOBAs like League of Legends. He has also occasionally dipped into tactical shooters like Counter-Strike 2, roguelikes like Hades, and hero shooters such as Overwatch and Marvel Rivals.

Chadley Kemp (preferably just "Chad") has nearly a decade of editorial experience spanning esports, gaming, crypto, and betting content, covering everything from Counter-Strike and VALORANT to League of Legends and Dota 2. Outside of esports, Chadley holds a Ph.D. in Physiology and has published research in several peer-reviewed scientific journals.

TheLeague of Legendspro circuit used to have a drafting problem, but hasFearless Draftactually changed that?

In the past, you could finish game 1 of a best-of-five, load into game 2, and see half of the same champions again. Maybe they swapped sides or banned a priority pick, but more often than not, you are basically watching another version of the same draft.

Even at Worlds, things could get stale by the time we reached the knockout stage. Teams end up handshaking drafts, and suddenly, we’re watching the same boringCorkivs.Azirmatchup in mid lane over and over again. Fearless Draft was supposed to change that.

On paper, the format inevitably creates variety. If a best-of-five series reaches game 5, 40 champions have already been removed through the previous picks before the regular bans even begin. But that raises a more interesting question:

title: South Korea National Esports Team Holds Send-off Ceremony for Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on the 25th
summary: South Korea National Esports Team Holds Send-off Ceremony for Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on the 25th  Inven Global
content:
On August 25, the send-off ceremony for the South Korean national esports team competing in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games was held at the Sangam Cube Convention Center in Mapo, Seoul. All 41 athletes and coaches competing across nine titles—including League of Legends, Tekken 8, and PUBG Mobile—attended the ceremony, solidifying their resolve to hunt for medals.

The event began with introductions of the national team athletes and coaches for each title, followed by a send-off report from the association detailing the selection process, operational progress, and local support plans, along with sponsor introductions and media interviews. The roster of national team athletes and coaches competing in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games for each title is as follows:

■ League of Legends: Head Coach Kang Dong-hoon, Choi Woo-je, Kim Geon-bu, Kim Geon-woo, Lee Sang-hyeok, Lee Min-hyeong, Ryu Min-seok

■ Fighting Games: Head Coach Kang Seong-hun, Yeon Je-gil (Street Fighter 6), Bae Jae-min (Tekken 8), Lee Gwang-no (The King of Fighters XV)

■ Pokémon UNITE: Kim Jae-young, Park Seong-soon, Lee Ji-hwan, Jin Soo-bin, Cho Min-hyuk

■ Honor of Kings: Head Coach Jang Hyeong-jun, Cho Seong-bin, Han Ji-hoon, Lee Seob-gyu, Jeong Yun-ho, Lee Hoon-min, Han Seong-geon

title: Esports World Cup Pulled in a Massive 850 Million Viewers in 2026
summary: Esports World Cup Pulled in a Massive 850 Million Viewers in 2026  Insider Gaming
content:
The Esports World Cup wenthugethis year, racking up a monumental count of 850million viewersand a staggering 440million hours watched, the EWC Foundation has revealed. That represents year-over-year growth of 13% and 26%, respectively, but the real gem comes from ticket sales:up 94% in Paris compared to 2025 in Riyadh.

During the event, more thantwo million peoplevisited an Esports World Cup tournament or activation, making this a record-shattering competitive gaming event that will go down in the history books formanyreasons.

To close out the Esports World Cup in Paris, France, AG.AL lifted the ultimate Club Champion trophy, securing a whopping prize worth $7 million, along with a coveted trophy that marked the organization as thebest of the best.

The organization’s competitors secured wins in Trackmania and TEKKEN 8, and second-place finishes in Chess, Free Fire, and Honor of Kings, and a third-place finish in Teamfight Tactics. That was enough to garner the points necessary to win the sought-after Club Chamnpionship.

On stage in Paris, President Emmanuel Macron handed the team the trophy alongside HRH Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. Ina statement, Ralf Reichert, the CEO of the Esports Foundation, said:

Our ambition has always been bigger than a single event: to grow esports and establish it as a leading global sport.
